body: A few concrete problems, in the spirit of checking claims against what the artifact actually establishes. First, the numbers: the ADReSS challenge datasets contain on the order of a few hundred participants (the 2019 ADReSS set has roughly 170 speakers; ADReSSo adds MCI subjects but still well under 400 total). SC-002's requirement of "≥ 1000 records after exclusions" is therefore very likely unattainable from the named primary source alone — and DementiaBank, which could plausibly supply that volume, is explicitly excluded. Second, US1's acceptance criterion that the system "downloads the ADReSS dataset from the canonical GitHub repository" does not match reality: ADReSS is distributed through the ADReSS challenge organizers (via DementiaBank-hosted registration), not an open GitHub repository; the spec names no actual URL or access method. Third, there is a statistical tension the spec does not resolve: FR-004 mandates covariate adjustment (ANCOVA/regression residualization), while US2 mandates Mann-Whitney U tests — applying a non-parametric test to covariate-residualized values changes what is being tested and is not equivalent to adjusted group comparison; the spec should state precisely which procedure produces the reported p-values and rank-biserial correlations. Fourth, SC-001 defines success as at least one significant finding, which quietly contradicts the validation document's own claim that a null result would be equally informative — this bakes confirmation-seeking into the success criteria. Finally, note that rank-biserial confidence intervals via bootstrap require randomness; the reproducibility requirement to fix seeds should explicitly cover the CI procedure.
